title: The Adventures of Superman
paragraphs: Juvenile superhero adventure serial based on the Superman comic-book character. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 171 dated early-run recordings from February 12, 1940 through March 17, 1941, well before the later wartime/anti-intolerance period.

GRH documents the program through Early 15-minute serial (February 12, 1940 to 1942) on [[org|org.ff9e40da2345dc9d|WOR]], Mutual weekday serial (August 31, 1942 to January 28, 1949) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Mutual 30-minute era (January 31, 1949 to June 17, 1949) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and ABC final era (November 5, 1949 to March 1, 1951) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include treasure, gems and valuable objects, crime, gangs and sabotage, disaster and rescue, science, inventions and experimental technology, ships, sea travel and maritime danger, and aircraft and aviation danger.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic-book superhero enters serialized radio, Wartime-era youth adventure broadcasting, and Radio superhero used for anti-intolerance messaging.
plain_text:
Juvenile superhero adventure serial based on the Superman comic-book character. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 171 dated early-run recordings from February 12, 1940 through March 17, 1941, well before the later wartime/anti-intolerance period.

GRH documents the program through Early 15-minute serial (February 12, 1940 to 1942) on WOR, Mutual weekday serial (August 31, 1942 to January 28, 1949) on Mutual Broadcasting System, Mutual 30-minute era (January 31, 1949 to June 17, 1949) on Mutual Broadcasting System, and ABC final era (November 5, 1949 to March 1, 1951) on ABC Radio Network.

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include treasure, gems and valuable objects, crime, gangs and sabotage, disaster and rescue, science, inventions and experimental technology, ships, sea travel and maritime danger, and aircraft and aviation danger.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic-book superhero enters serialized radio, Wartime-era youth adventure broadcasting, and Radio superhero used for anti-intolerance messaging.
